- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 3–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates drop; add 2–5% buffer below true low.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending sideways, model often misreads mean reversion; align forecast to 20-day moving average.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging; if sentiment is strong, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lead-in to true price action.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% in such cases.
